_notes.languages: autoLanguages = languages the species always knows (shown as granted, not re-selectable). language_choice features let them pick additional ones.
_notes.abilityBonusChoices: Use asi_points type feature instead of the old abilityBonusChoices field. Set 'points' to total points to spend, 'exclude' to ability keys that can't receive points.
_notes.subclasses: Each class can have a 'subclasses' object. Key = subclass name, value = object with 'features' array (same format).

Blue — Lightning (5 by 30 ft. line, Dex save)
Brass — Fire (5 by 30 ft. line, Dex save)
Bronze — Lightning (5 by 30 ft. line, Dex save)
Copper — Acid (5 by 30 ft. line, Dex save)

Green — Poison (15 ft. cone, Con save)
Red — Fire (15 ft. cone, Dex save)

features.name: Breath Weapon
features.description: You can use your action to exhale destructive energy. Your draconic ancestry determines the size, shape, and damage type of the exhalation. When you use your breath weapon, each creature in the area of the exhalation must make a saving throw, the type of which is determined by your draconic ancestry. The DC for this saving throw equals 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. A creature takes 2d6 damage on a failed save, and half as much damage on a successful one. The damage increases to 3d6 at 6th level, 4d6 at 11th level, and 5d6 at 16th level. After you use your breath weapon, you can't use it again until you complete a short or long rest.
features.note: Exhale energy in a cone or line; DEX save for half damage

features.name: Damage Resistance
features.description: You have resistance to the damage type associated with your draconic ancestry.

features.name: Darkvision
features.description: Blessed with a radiant soul, your vision can easily cut through darkness. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light.

features.name: Celestial Resistance
features.description: You have resistance to necrotic damage and radiant damage.

features.name: Healing Hands
features.description: As an action, you can touch a creature and cause it to regain hit points equal to your level. Once per long rest.
features.note: Touch a creature; restore HP equal to your level

features.name: Light Bearer
features.description: You know the Light cantrip. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it.

features.name: Hit Points
features.description: Hit Dice: 1d12 per Barbarian level. HP at 1st level: 12 + Constitution modifier. HP at higher levels: 1d12 (or 7) + Constitution modifier per level above 1st.

features.name: Proficiencies
features.description: Armor: Light, Medium, Shields. Weapons: Simple, Martial. Saving Throws: Strength, Constitution. Skills: Choose 2 from Animal Handling, Athletics, Intimidation, Nature, Perception, Survival.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: Choose 2 skills from the Barbarian list.

features.name: Rage
features.description: In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action. While raging you gain advantage on Strength checks and saving throws, a bonus to damage rolls, and resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. You can rage 2 times per long rest at 1st level, increasing as you level up.
features.note: Advantage on STR checks/saves, resistance to B/P/S damage

features.name: Unarmored Defense
features.description: While you are not wearing any armor, your AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

features.name: Reckless Attack
features.description: Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly, giving you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.
features.note: Advantage on STR attacks this turn; attacks against you have advantage

features.name: Danger Sense
features.description: At 2nd level, you gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge away from danger. You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells.

features.name: Primal Path
features.description: At 3rd level, you choose a path that shapes the nature of your rage.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.description: You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. You can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
features.note: Attack twice instead of once when you take the Attack action

features.name: Fast Movement
features.description: Starting at 5th level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing heavy armor.

features.name: Feral Instinct
features.description: By 7th level, your instincts are so honed that you have advantage on initiative rolls. Additionally, if you are surprised at the beginning of combat and aren't incapacitated, you can act normally on your first turn, but only if you enter your rage before doing anything else on that turn.

features.name: Brutal Critical
features.description: Beginning at 9th level, you can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack. This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three additional dice at 17th level.

features.name: Relentless Rage
features.description: Starting at 11th level, your rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 hit points while you're raging and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, you drop to 1 hit point instead.

features.name: Persistent Rage
features.description: Beginning at 15th level, your rage is so fierce that it ends early only if you fall unconscious or if you choose to end it.

features.name: Indomitable Might
features.description: Beginning at 18th level, if your total for a Strength check is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

features.name: Primal Champion
features.description: At 20th level, you embody the power of the wilds. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4. Your maximum for those scores is now 24.

features.name: Frenzy
features.description: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can go into a frenzy when you rage. If you do so, for the duration of your rage you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one.

features.name: Mindless Rage
features.description: Beginning at 6th level, you can't be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are charmed or frightened when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of the rage.

features.name: Intimidating Presence
features.description: Beginning at 10th level, you can use your action to frighten someone with your menacing presence.

features.name: Retaliation
features.description: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature.

features.name: Spirit Seeker
features.description: Yours is a path that seeks attunement with the natural world, giving you a kinship with beasts. At 3rd level you gain the ability to cast the Beast Sense and Speak with Animals spells as rituals.

features.name: Totem Spirit
features.description: At 3rd level, when you adopt this path, you choose a totem spirit and gain its feature.
options: Bear — While raging you have resistance to all damage except psychic
Eagle — While raging you are difficult to track and can Dash as a bonus action
Wolf — While raging your friends have advantage on melee attack rolls against creatures adjacent to you

features.name: Aspect of the Beast
features.description: At 6th level, you gain a magical benefit based on the totem animal of your choice.
options: Eagle — You can see up to 1 mile with perfect clarity
Wolf — You can track other creatures while traveling at a fast pace

features.name: Totemic Attunement
features.description: At 14th level, you gain a magical benefit based on a totem animal of your choice.
options: Bear — While raging, any creature within 5 ft has disadvantage on attacks not against you
Eagle — While raging you have a flying speed equal to your current walking speed
Wolf — While raging you can use a bonus action to knock a Large or smaller creature prone

features.name: Hit Points
features.description: Hit Dice: 1d8 per Rogue level. HP at 1st level: 8 + Constitution modifier. HP at higher levels: 1d8 (or 5) + Constitution modifier per level above 1st.

features.name: Proficiencies
features.description: Armor: Light. Weapons: Simple, Hand Crossbows, Longswords, Rapiers, Shortswords. Tools: Thieves' Tools. Saving Throws: Dexterity, Intelligence.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: Choose 4 skills from the Rogue list.

features.name: Expertise
features.description: At 1st level, choose two of your skill proficiencies, or one of your skill proficiencies and your proficiency with thieves' tools. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.

features.name: Sneak Attack
features.description: Beginning at 1st level, you know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. This extra damage increases as you gain Rogue levels: 2d6 at 3rd, 3d6 at 5th, 4d6 at 7th, 5d6 at 9th...
features.note: Once per turn on attack with advantage or with ally adjacent to target

features.name: Thieves' Cant
features.description: During your rogue training you learned thieves' cant, a secret mix of dialect, jargon, and code that allows you to hide messages in seemingly normal conversation. It takes four times longer to convey such a message than it does to speak the same idea plainly.

features.name: Cunning Action
features.description: Starting at 2nd level, your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. You can take a bonus action on each of your turns in combat. This action can be used only to take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.
features.note: Dash, Disengage, or Hide as a bonus action

features.name: Roguish Archetype
features.description: At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you emulate in the exercise of your rogue abilities.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.description: You can increase one ability score by 2, or two ability scores by 1 each. You can't exceed 20.

features.name: Uncanny Dodge
features.description: Starting at 5th level, when an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.
features.note: Halve damage from one attack you can see

features.name: Expertise (2nd)
features.description: At 6th level, choose two more of your skill proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for those skills.

features.name: Evasion
features.description: Beginning at 7th level, you can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain area effects. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

features.name: Reliable Talent
features.description: By 11th level, you have refined your chosen skills until they approach perfection. Whenever you make an ability check that lets you add your proficiency bonus, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

features.name: Blindsense
features.description: Starting at 14th level, if you are able to hear, you are aware of the location of any hidden or invisible creature within 10 feet of you.

features.name: Slippery Mind
features.description: By 15th level, you have acquired greater mental strength. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.

features.name: Elusive
features.description: Beginning at 18th level, you are so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll has advantage against you while you aren't incapacitated.

features.name: Stroke of Luck
features.description: At 20th level, you have an uncanny knack for succeeding when you need to. If your attack misses a target within range, you can turn the miss into a hit. Alternatively, if you fail an ability check, you can treat the d20 roll as a 20. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Fast Hands
features.description: Starting at 3rd level, you can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, use your thieves' tools to disarm a trap or open a lock, or take the Use an Object action.

features.name: Second-Story Work
features.description: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain the ability to climb faster than normal; climbing no longer costs you extra movement. Additionally, when you make a running jump, the distance you cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Dexterity modifier.

features.name: Supreme Sneak
features.description: Starting at 9th level, you have advantage on a Dexterity (Stealth) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.

features.name: Use Magic Device
features.description: By 13th level, you have learned enough about the workings of magic that you can improvise the use of items even when they are not intended for you. You ignore all class, race, and level requirements on the use of magic items.

features.name: Thief's Reflexes
features.description: When you reach 17th level, you have become adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal initiative and your second turn at your initiative minus 10.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.description: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with the disguise kit and the poisoner's kit.

features.name: Assassinate
features.description: Starting at 3rd level, you are at your deadliest when you get the drop on your enemies. You have advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn in the combat yet. In addition, any hit you score against a creature that is surprised is a critical hit.

features.name: Infiltration Expertise
features.description: Starting at 9th level, you can unfailingly create false identities for yourself.

features.name: Impostor
features.description: At 13th level, you gain the ability to unerringly mimic another person's speech, writing, and behavior.

features.name: Death Strike
features.description: Starting at 17th level, you become a master of instant death. When you attack and hit a creature that is surprised, it must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your Dexterity modifier + your proficiency bonus). On a failed save, double the damage of your attack against the creature.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: When you reach 3rd level, you augment your martial prowess with the ability to cast spells. You learn 3 cantrips (Mage Hand plus 2 others from the wizard list) and 3 1st-level spells from the enchantment or illusion schools.

features.name: Mage Hand Legerdemain
features.description: Starting at 3rd level, when you cast Mage Hand, you can make the spectral hand invisible, and you can perform the following additional tasks with it.

features.name: Magical Ambush
features.description: Starting at 9th level, if you are hidden from a creature when you cast a spell on it, the creature has disadvantage on any saving throw it makes against the spell this turn.

features.name: Versatile Trickster
features.description: At 13th level, you gain the ability to distract targets with your Mage Hand. As a bonus action on your turn, you can designate a creature within 5 feet of the spectral hand created by the spell. Doing so gives you advantage on attack rolls against that creature until the end of the turn.

features.name: Spell Thief
features.description: At 17th level, you gain the ability to magically steal the knowledge of how to cast a spell from another spellcaster.

features.name: Fighting Style
features.description: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options.

Defense — +1 bonus to AC when wearing armor
Dueling — +2 damage when wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons
Great Weapon Fighting — Reroll 1s and 2s on damage dice for two-handed weapons
Protection — Use reaction to impose disadvantage on an attack against an adjacent ally
Two-Weapon Fighting — Add ability modifier to off-hand attack damage

features.name: Second Wind
features.description: You have a limited well of stamina that you can draw on to protect yourself from harm. On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your fighter level. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.
features.note: Regain 1d10 + Fighter level HP

features.name: Action Surge
features.description: Starting at 2nd level, you can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again. Starting at 17th level, you can use it twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.
features.note: Take one additional action this turn

features.description: You can attack three times when you take the Attack action.
features.note: Attack three times when you take the Attack action

features.note: Attack four times when you take the Attack action

features.description: Beginning when you choose this archetype at 3rd level, your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

features.name: Remarkable Athlete
features.description: Starting at 7th level, you can add half your proficiency bonus (rounded up) to any Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution check you make that doesn't already use your proficiency bonus.

features.name: Additional Fighting Style
features.description: At 10th level, you can choose a second option from the Fighting Style class feature.

features.name: Superior Critical
features.description: Starting at 15th level, your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18–20.

features.name: Survivor

features.name: Combat Superiority
features.description: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called superiority dice (d8s). You have 4, gaining more as you level up.

features.name: Maneuvers
features.description: You learn 3 maneuvers of your choice. You learn 2 additional maneuvers at 7th, 10th, and 15th level.

features.name: Know Your Enemy
features.description: Starting at 7th level, if you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your own.

features.name: Relentless
features.description: Starting at 15th level, when you roll initiative and have no superiority dice remaining, you regain one superiority die.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: When you reach 3rd level, you augment your martial prowess with the ability to cast spells. You learn 2 cantrips from the wizard spell list and 3 first-level spells from the abjuration or evocation schools.

features.name: War Magic
features.description: Beginning at 7th level, when you use your action to cast a cantrip, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

features.name: Eldritch Strike
features.description: At 10th level, you learn how to make your weapon strikes undercut a creature's resistance to your spells. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, that creature has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes against a spell you cast before the end of your next turn.

features.name: Arcane Charge
features.description: At 15th level, you gain the ability to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see when you use your Action Surge.

features.description: Hit Dice: 1d6 per Wizard level. HP at 1st level: 6 + Constitution modifier.

features.name: Proficiencies
features.description: Weapons: Daggers, Darts, Slings, Quarterstaffs, Light Crossbows. Saving Throws: Intelligence, Wisdom.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: Choose 2 skills from the Wizard list.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: As a student of arcane magic, you have a spellbook containing spells that show the first glimmerings of your true power. Your spellcasting ability is Intelligence.

features.name: Arcane Recovery
features.description: You have learned to regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. Once per day when you finish a short rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your wizard level (rounded up).

features.name: Arcane Tradition
features.description: When you reach 2nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic through one of eight schools.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.description: You can increase one ability score by 2, or two ability scores by 1 each.

features.name: Spell Mastery
features.description: At 18th level, you have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a 1st-level wizard spell and a 2nd-level wizard spell that are in your spellbook. You can cast those spells at their lowest level without expending a spell slot when you have them prepared.

features.name: Signature Spells
features.description: When you reach 20th level, you gain mastery over two powerful spells and can cast them with little effort. Choose two 3rd-level wizard spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, they don't count against the number of spells you have prepared, and you can cast each of them once at 3rd level without expending a spell slot.

features.name: Evocation Savant
features.description: Beginning when you select this school at 2nd level, the gold and time you must spend to copy an evocation spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Sculpt Spells
features.description: Beginning at 2nd level, you can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocation spells. When you cast an evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

features.name: Potent Cantrip
features.description: Starting at 6th level, your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your cantrip, the creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

features.name: Empowered Evocation
features.description: Beginning at 10th level, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast.

features.name: Abjuration Savant
features.description: The gold and time you must spend to copy an abjuration spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Arcane Ward
features.description: Starting at 2nd level, you can weave magic around yourself for protection. When you cast an abjuration spell of 1st level or higher, you can simultaneously use a strand of the spell's magic to create a magical ward on yourself that lasts until you finish a long rest. The ward has hit points equal to twice your wizard level + your Intelligence modifier.

features.name: Projected Ward
features.description: Starting at 6th level, when a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to cause your Arcane Ward to absorb that damage.

features.name: Improved Abjuration
features.description: Beginning at 10th level, when you cast an abjuration spell that requires you to make an ability check as a part of casting that spell, you add your proficiency bonus to that ability check.

features.name: Hit Points
features.description: Hit Dice: 1d8 per Cleric level. HP at 1st level: 8 + Constitution modifier.

features.name: Proficiencies
features.description: Armor: Light, Medium, Shields. Weapons: Simple. Saving Throws: Wisdom, Charisma.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: Choose 2 skills from the Cleric list.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: As a conduit for divine power, you can cast cleric spells. Your spellcasting ability is Wisdom.

features.name: Divine Domain
features.description: Choose one domain related to your deity. Your choice grants you domain spells and other features when you choose it at 1st level.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: At 2nd level, you gain the ability to channel divine energy directly from your deity, using that energy to fuel magical effects. You start with two such effects: Turn Undead and an effect determined by your domain. You can use Channel Divinity once between short rests (twice at 6th, three times at 18th).

features.name: Destroy Undead
features.description: Starting at 5th level, when an undead fails its saving throw against your Turn Undead feature, the creature is instantly destroyed if its challenge rating is at or below a certain threshold.

features.name: Divine Intervention
features.description: Beginning at 10th level, you can call on your deity to intervene on your behalf when your need is great. Imploring your deity's aid requires you to use your action. Describe the assistance you seek, and roll percentile dice. If you roll a number equal to or lower than your cleric level, your deity intervenes.
features.note: Roll d100; if ≤ cleric level, deity intervenes

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
features.description: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.

features.name: Disciple of Life
features.description: Also starting at 1st level, your healing spells are more effective. Whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, the creature regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
features.description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to heal the badly injured. As an action, you present your holy symbol and evoke healing energy that can restore a number of hit points equal to five times your cleric level.

features.name: Blessed Healer
features.description: Beginning at 6th level, the healing spells you cast on others heal you as well. When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.description: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage to the target.

features.name: Supreme Healing
features.description: Starting at 17th level, when you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die.

features.name: Hit Points
features.description: Hit Dice: 1d8 per Bard level. HP at 1st level: 8 + Constitution modifier.

features.name: Proficiencies
features.description: Armor: Light. Weapons: Simple, Hand Crossbows, Longswords, Rapiers, Shortswords. Tools: Three musical instruments. Saving Throws: Dexterity, Charisma.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: Choose any 3 skills.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: You have learned to untangle and reshape the fabric of reality in harmony with your wishes and music. Your spellcasting ability is Charisma.

features.name: Bardic Inspiration
features.description: You can inspire others through stirring words or music. To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die, a d6. This increases to d8 at 5th level, d10 at 10th, and d12 at 15th.
features.note: Grant a creature a Bardic Inspiration die (d6–d12)

features.name: Jack of All Trades
features.description: Starting at 2nd level, you can add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any ability check you make that doesn't already include your proficiency bonus.

features.name: Expertise
features.description: At 3rd level, choose two of your skill proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.

features.name: Bard College
features.description: At 3rd level, you delve into the advanced techniques of a bard college of your choice.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.description: You can increase one ability score by 2, or two ability scores by 1 each.

features.name: Font of Inspiration
features.description: Beginning when you reach 5th level, you regain all of your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Countercharm
features.description: At 6th level, you gain the ability to use musical notes or words of power to disrupt mind-influencing effects. As an action, you can start a performance that lasts until the end of your next turn. During that time, you and any friendly creatures within 30 feet of you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed.
features.note: Grant advantage on saves vs being frightened/charmed to nearby allies

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.description: When you join the College of Lore at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

features.name: Cutting Words
features.description: Also at 3rd level, you learn how to use your wit to distract, confuse, and otherwise sap the confidence and competence of others.

features.name: Additional Magical Secrets
features.description: At 6th level, you learn two spells of your choice from any class. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip.

features.name: Peerless Skill
features.description: Starting at 14th level, when you make an ability check, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration. Roll a Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to your ability check.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.description: When you join the College of Valor at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons.

features.name: Combat Inspiration
features.description: Also at 3rd level, you learn to inspire others in battle. A creature that has a Bardic Inspiration die from you can roll that die and add the number rolled to a weapon damage roll it just made.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.description: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
features.note: Attack twice instead of once when you take the Attack action

features.name: Battle Magic
features.description: At 14th level, you have mastered the art of weaving spellcasting and weapon use into a single harmonious act. When you use your action to cast a bard spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

options.name: Diplomat's Pack
options.description: Chest, 2 cases for maps/scrolls, fine clothes, bottle of ink, ink pen, lamp, 2 flasks oil, 5 sheets paper, vial perfume, sealing wax, soap

options.name: Entertainer's Pack
options.description: Backpack, bedroll, 2 costumes, 5 candles, 5 days rations, waterskin, disguise kit

features.name: Hit Points
features.description: Hit Dice: 1d10 per Paladin level. HP at 1st level: 10 + Constitution modifier.

features.name: Proficiencies
features.description: Armor: All armor, Shields. Weapons: Simple, Martial. Saving Throws: Wisdom, Charisma.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: Choose 2 skills from the Paladin list.

features.name: Divine Sense
features.description: The presence of strong evil registers on your senses like a noxious odor, and powerful good rings like heavenly music in your ears. As an action, you can open your awareness to detect such forces until the end of your next turn.
features.note: Detect celestials, fiends, undead within 60 ft

features.name: Lay on Hands
features.description: Your blessed touch can heal wounds. You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you take a long rest. With that pool, you can restore a total number of hit points equal to your paladin level × 5.
features.note: Restore HP from a pool equal to 5 × Paladin level

features.name: Fighting Style
features.description: At 2nd level, you adopt a style of fighting as your specialty.
options: Dueling — +2 damage with one-handed melee weapon
Great Weapon Fighting — Reroll 1s and 2s on damage for two-handed weapons
Protection — Impose disadvantage on attacks against adjacent allies

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: By 2nd level, you have learned to draw on divine magic through meditation and prayer to cast spells as a cleric does. Your spellcasting ability is Charisma.

features.name: Divine Smite
features.description: Starting at 2nd level, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one spell slot to deal radiant damage to the target, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is 2d8 for a 1st-level spell slot, plus 1d8 for each spell level higher than 1st, to a maximum of 5d8.
features.note: On melee hit, expend spell slot for 2d8 + 1d8/slot radiant damage

features.name: Sacred Oath
features.description: When you reach 3rd level, you swear the oath that binds you as a paladin forever. Up to this time you have been in a preparatory stage, committed to the path but not yet sworn to it.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
features.note: Attack twice instead of once when you take the Attack action

features.name: Aura of Protection
features.description: Starting at 6th level, whenever you or a friendly creature within 10 feet of you must make a saving throw, the creature gains a bonus to the saving throw equal to your Charisma modifier (with a minimum bonus of +1). You must be conscious to grant this bonus.

features.name: Aura of Courage
features.description: Starting at 10th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be frightened while you are conscious.

features.name: Sacred Weapon
features.description: As an action, you can imbue one weapon that you are holding with positive energy, using your Channel Divinity. For 1 minute, you add your Charisma modifier to attack rolls made with that weapon (with a minimum bonus of +1).

features.name: Turn the Unholy
features.description: As an action, you present your holy symbol and speak a prayer censuring fiends and undead, using your Channel Divinity. Each fiend or undead that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw.

features.name: Aura of Devotion
features.description: Starting at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be charmed while you are conscious.

features.name: Natural Explorer
features.description: You are particularly familiar with one type of natural environment and are adept at traveling and surviving in such regions.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: By the time you reach 2nd level, you have learned to use the magical essence of nature to cast spells, much as a druid does. Your spellcasting ability is Wisdom.

features.name: Ranger Archetype
features.description: At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you strive to emulate: Hunter or Beast Master.

features.name: Extra Attack

features.note: Attack twice instead of once when you take the Attack action

features.name: Hunter's Prey
features.description: At 3rd level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
options: Colossus Slayer — Extra 1d8 damage to damaged creatures once per turn
Giant Killer — Reaction attack when an adjacent Large+ creature misses you
Horde Breaker — Attack a second adjacent creature with the same weapon once per turn

features.name: Defensive Tactics
features.description: At 7th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
options: Escape the Horde — Opportunity attacks against you have disadvantage
Multiattack Defense — +4 to AC after being hit until the end of the attacker's turn
Steel Will — Advantage on saves against being frightened

features.name: Multiattack
features.description: At 11th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
options: Volley — Attack every creature in a 10-ft radius you can see (ranged)
Whirlwind Attack — Melee attack against any number of adjacent creatures

features.name: Druidic
features.description: You know Druidic, the secret language of druids. You can speak the language and use it to leave hidden messages.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: Drawing on the divine essence of nature itself, you can cast spells to shape that essence to your will. Your spellcasting ability is Wisdom.

features.name: Wild Shape
features.description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your action to magically assume the shape of a beast that you have seen before. You can use this feature twice, regaining uses on a short or long rest.
features.note: Transform into a beast you have seen

features.name: Druid Circle
features.description: At 2nd level, you choose to identify with a circle of druids.

features.name: Timeless Body
features.description: Starting at 18th level, the primal magic that you wield causes you to age more slowly. For every 10 years that pass, your body ages only 1 year.

features.name: Beast Spells
features.description: Beginning at 18th level, you can cast many of your druid spells in any shape you assume using Wild Shape.

features.name: Archdruid
features.description: At 20th level, you can use your Wild Shape an unlimited number of times.

features.name: Bonus Cantrip
features.description: When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you learn one additional druid cantrip of your choice.

features.name: Natural Recovery
features.description: Starting at 2nd level, you can regain some of your magical energy by sitting in meditation and communing with nature. During a short rest, you choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your druid level (rounded up).

features.name: Circle Spells
features.description: Your mystical connection to the land infuses you with the ability to cast certain spells. Choose the type of land.

features.name: Unarmored Defense
features.description: Beginning at 1st level, while you are wearing no armor and not wielding a shield, your AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier.

features.name: Martial Arts
features.description: At 1st level, your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use unarmed strikes and monk weapons. You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for attack and damage rolls, and your unarmed strike deals 1d4 (increasing with level).
features.note: After Attack action with unarmed/monk weapon, make one unarmed strike

features.name: Ki
features.description: Starting at 2nd level, your training allows you to harness the mystic energy of ki. Your access to this energy is represented by a number of ki points. You have ki points equal to your monk level.

features.name: Monastic Tradition
features.description: When you reach 3rd level, you commit yourself to a monastic tradition.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement

features.name: Extra Attack

features.note: Attack twice instead of once when you take the Attack action

features.name: Stunning Strike
features.description: Starting at 5th level, you can interfere with the flow of ki in an opponent's body. When you hit another creature with a melee weapon attack, you can spend 1 ki point to attempt a stunning strike.
features.note: On hit, spend 1 ki point; target makes CON save or is stunned until your next turn

features.name: Open Hand Technique
features.description: Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you can manipulate your enemy's ki when you harness your own. Whenever you hit a creature with one of the attacks granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following effects on that target.

features.name: Wholeness of Body
features.description: At 6th level, you gain the ability to heal yourself. As an action, you can regain hit points equal to three times your monk level. You must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again.

features.name: Tranquility
features.description: Beginning at 11th level, you can enter a special meditation that surrounds you with an aura of peace.

features.name: Quivering Palm
features.description: At 17th level, you gain the ability to set up lethal vibrations in someone's body.

features.name: Proficiencies

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: Choose 2 skills from the Sorcerer list.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: An event in your past, or in the life of a parent or ancestor, left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with arcane magic. Your spellcasting ability is Charisma.

features.name: Sorcerous Origin
features.description: Choose a sorcerous origin, which describes the source of your innate magical power.

features.name: Font of Magic
features.description: At 2nd level, you tap into a deep wellspring of magic within yourself. This wellspring is represented by sorcery points, which allow you to create a variety of magical effects. You have 2 sorcery points at 2nd level, and you gain one more sorcery point every time you level up, to a maximum of 20 at level 20.

features.name: Metamagic
features.description: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to twist your spells to suit your needs. Choose two Metamagic options.

features.name: Dragon Ancestor
features.description: At 1st level, you choose one type of dragon as your ancestor. The damage type associated with each dragon is used by features you gain later.

features.name: Draconic Resilience
features.description: As magic flows through your body, it causes physical traits of your dragon ancestors to emerge. At 1st level, your hit point maximum increases by 1 and increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level in this class. Additionally, parts of your skin are covered by a thin sheen of dragon-like scales. When you aren't wearing armor, your AC equals 13 + your Dexterity modifier.

features.name: Elemental Affinity
features.description: Starting at 6th level, when you cast a spell that deals damage of the type associated with your draconic ancestry, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell.

features.name: Dragon Wings
features.description: At 14th level, you gain the ability to sprout a pair of dragon wings from your back, gaining a flying speed equal to your current speed.

features.name: Wild Magic Surge
features.description: Starting when you choose this origin at 1st level, your spellcasting can unleash surges of untamed magic. Immediately after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, the DM can have you roll a d20. If you roll a 1, roll on the Wild Magic Surge table.

features.name: Tides of Chaos
features.description: Starting at 1st level, you can manipulate the forces of chance and chaos to gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. Once you do so, you must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again.

features.name: Bend Luck
features.description: Starting at 6th level, you have the ability to twist fate using your wild magic. When another creature you can see makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction and spend 2 sorcery points to roll 1d4 and apply the number rolled as a bonus or penalty (your choice) to the creature's roll.

features.name: Hit Points
features.description: Hit Dice: 1d8 per Warlock level. Hit Points at 1st Level: 8 + your Constitution modifier. Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per Warlock level after 1st.

features.name: Proficiencies
features.description: Armor: Light armor. Weapons: Simple weapons. Tools: None. Saving Throws: Wisdom, Charisma. Skills: Choose 2 from Arcana, Deception, History, Intimidation, Investigation, Nature, and Religion.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: Choose 2 skills from the Warlock list.

features.name: Otherworldly Patron
features.description: You have struck a bargain with an otherworldly being. Your choice of patron shapes your Expanded Spell List, and grants you features at 1st, 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

features.name: Pact Magic
features.description: Your arcane research and the magic bestowed on you by your patron have given you facility with spells. You have a number of pact magic spell slots determined by your level. All your slots are the same level (pact slot level). You regain all expended slots on a short or long rest. You know a number of spells equal to your Warlock level, choosing from the Warlock spell list (plus your Patron's Expanded Spell List).

features.name: Eldritch Invocations
features.description: In your study of occult lore, you have unearthed Eldritch Invocations — fragments of forbidden knowledge. You gain 2 invocations at 2nd level. You gain an additional invocation at 5th, 7th, 9th, 12th, 15th, and 18th level. If an invocation has a prerequisite, you must meet it to learn that invocation. Whenever you gain a warlock level, you can replace one invocation with another.

invocations.name: Armor of Shadows
invocations.description: You can cast Mage Armor on yourself at will, without expending a spell slot or material components.

invocations.name: Beast Speech
invocations.description: You can cast Speak with Animals at will, without expending a spell slot.

invocations.name: Beguiling Influence
invocations.description: You gain proficiency in the Deception and Persuasion skills.

invocations.name: Devil's Sight
invocations.description: You can see normally in darkness, both magical and nonmagical, to a distance of 120 feet.

invocations.name: Eldritch Mind
invocations.description: You have advantage on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain your concentration on a spell.

invocations.name: Eldritch Sight
invocations.description: You can cast Detect Magic at will, without expending a spell slot.

invocations.name: Eyes of the Rune Keeper
invocations.description: You can read all writing.

invocations.name: Fiendish Vigor
invocations.description: You can cast False Life on yourself at will as a 1st-level spell, without expending a spell slot or material components.

invocations.name: Gaze of Two Minds
invocations.description: You can use your action to touch a willing humanoid and perceive through its senses until the end of your next turn.

invocations.name: Mask of Many Faces
invocations.description: You can cast Disguise Self at will, without expending a spell slot.

invocations.name: Misty Visions
invocations.description: You can cast Silent Image at will, without expending a spell slot or material components.

invocations.name: Thief of Five Fates
invocations.description: You can cast Bane once using a warlock spell slot. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

invocations.name: Agonizing Blast
invocations.description: When you cast Eldritch Blast, add your Charisma modifier to the damage it deals on a hit.

invocations.name: Lance of Lethargy
invocations.description: Once per turn when you hit a creature with your Eldritch Blast, you can reduce that creature's speed by 10 feet until the end of your next turn.

invocations.name: Repelling Blast
invocations.description: When you hit a creature with Eldritch Blast, you can push the creature up to 10 feet away from you in a straight line.

invocations.name: Eldritch Spear
invocations.description: When you cast Eldritch Blast, its range is 300 feet.

invocations.name: Grasp of Hadar
invocations.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with your Eldritch Blast, you can move that creature in a straight line 10 feet closer to you.

invocations.name: One with Shadows
invocations.description: When you are in an area of dim light or darkness, you can use your action to become invisible until you move or take an action or a reaction.

invocations.name: Thirsting Blade
invocations.description: You can attack with your pact weapon twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

invocations.name: Tomb of Levistus
invocations.description: As a reaction when you take damage, you can entomb yourself in ice, which melts away at the end of your next turn. You gain 10 temporary hit points per warlock level, which take as much of the triggering damage as possible. You are then vulnerable to fire damage and restrained until the effect ends.

invocations.name: Undying Servitude
invocations.description: You can cast Animate Dead without using a spell slot. Once you do so, you can't cast it this way again until you finish a long rest.

invocations.name: Bewitching Whispers
invocations.description: You can cast Compulsion once using a warlock spell slot. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

invocations.name: Dreadful Word
invocations.description: You can cast Confusion once using a warlock spell slot. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

invocations.name: Sculptor of Flesh
invocations.description: You can cast Polymorph once using a warlock spell slot. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

invocations.name: Ascendant Step
invocations.description: You can cast Levitate on yourself at will, without expending a spell slot or material components.

invocations.name: Minions of Chaos
invocations.description: You can cast Conjure Elemental once using a warlock spell slot. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

invocations.name: Otherworldly Leap
invocations.description: You can cast Jump on yourself at will, without expending a spell slot or material components.

invocations.name: Improved Pact Weapon
invocations.description: You can use any weapon you summon with your Pact of the Blade feature as a spellcasting focus for your warlock spells. In addition, the weapon gains a +1 bonus to its attack and damage rolls, unless it is a magic weapon that already has a bonus to those rolls. Finally, the weapon you conjure can be a shortbow, longbow, light crossbow, or hand crossbow.

invocations.name: Gift of the Depths
invocations.description: You can breathe underwater, and you gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed. You can also cast Water Breathing without expending a spell slot. Once you do so, you can't cast it this way again until you finish a long rest.

invocations.name: Chains of Carceri
invocations.description: You can cast Hold Monster at will — targeting a celestial, fiend, or elemental — without expending a spell slot or material components. You must finish a long rest before you can use this invocation on the same creature again.

invocations.name: Shroud of Shadow
invocations.description: You can cast Invisibility at will, without expending a spell slot.

invocations.name: Witch Sight
invocations.description: You can see the true form of any shapechanger or creature concealed by illusion or transmutation magic while the creature is within 30 feet of you and within line of sight.

invocations.name: Voice of the Chain Master
invocations.description: You can communicate telepathically with your familiar and perceive through your familiar's senses as long as you are on the same plane of existence. Additionally, while perceiving through your familiar's senses, you can also speak through your familiar in your own voice, even if your familiar is normally incapable of speech.

invocations.name: Book of Ancient Secrets
invocations.description: You can inscribe magical rituals in your Book of Shadows. Choose two 1st-level spells that have the ritual tag from any class's spell list (e.g. Alarm, Detect Magic, Find Familiar, Identify, Illusory Script, Tenser's Floating Disk, Unseen Servant). The spells appear in the book and don't count against your spells known. With your Book of Shadows in hand, you can cast them as rituals. If you encounter a spell in written form, you can add it to your Book of Shadows if it is on any class's spell list, the spell's level is no higher than half your Warlock level (rounded up), and you spend 2 hours and 50 gp per spell level. Ritual spells: Alarm, Ceremony, Comprehend Languages, Detect Magic, Detect Poison and Disease, Find Familiar, Identify, Illusory Script, Speak with Animals, Tenser's Floating Disk, Unseen Servant, Animal Messenger, Beast Sense, Gentle Repose, Magic Mouth, Silence, Skywrite, Augury, Clairvoyance, Meld into Stone, Nondetection, Speak with Dead, Speak with Plants, Water Breathing, Water Walk, Divination, Leomund's Tiny Hut, Drawmij's Instant Summons, Planar Binding, Rary's Telepathic Bond, Forbiddance, Word of Recall.

subChoice.prompt: Note your chosen ritual spells in your character notes
subChoice.note: Choose 2 ritual spells from any class list to inscribe in your Book of Shadows.

invocations.name: Lifedrinker
invocations.description: When you hit a creature with your pact weapon, the creature takes extra necrotic damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1).

features.name: Pact Boon
options: Pact of the Blade — create a pact weapon in your hand as an action. You are proficient with it and can use it as a spellcasting focus. It counts as magical. You can transform a magic weapon into your pact weapon by performing a ritual over 1 hour.
Pact of the Chain — you learn Find Familiar and can summon special familiars: imp, pseudodragon, quasit, or sprite. Your familiar can attack as a bonus action instead of you.
Pact of the Tome — your patron gives you a Book of Shadows containing 3 cantrips from any class's spell list. They count as Warlock cantrips for you.
Pact of the Talisman — your patron gives you an amulet. When the wearer fails an ability check, they can add a d4 to the result. You can give it to another creature.
features.description: Your patron grants you a boon at 3rd level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.description: Increase one ability score by 2, or two ability scores by 1 each. Cannot exceed 20.

features.name: Mystic Arcanum (6th)
features.description: Your patron bestows upon you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one 6th-level spell from the Warlock spell list as this arcanum. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

features.name: Mystic Arcanum (7th)
features.description: Choose one 7th-level spell from the Warlock spell list as your arcanum. Once per long rest without a spell slot.

features.name: Mystic Arcanum (8th)
features.description: Choose one 8th-level spell from the Warlock spell list as your arcanum. Once per long rest without a spell slot.

features.name: Mystic Arcanum (9th)
features.description: Choose one 9th-level spell from the Warlock spell list as your arcanum. Once per long rest without a spell slot.

features.name: Eldritch Master
features.description: You can draw on your inner reserve of mystical power while entreating your patron to regain expended spell slots. You can spend 1 minute entreating your patron for aid to regain all your expended pact magic spell slots. Once you regain spell slots with this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

features.name: Expanded Spell List (Fiend)
features.description: The Fiend lets you choose from an expanded list of spells. Fiend Expanded Spells: 1st: Burning Hands, Command; 2nd: Blindness/Deafness, Scorching Ray; 3rd: Fireball, Stinking Cloud; 4th: Fire Shield, Wall of Fire; 5th: Flame Strike, Hallow.

features.name: Dark One's Blessing
features.description: Starting at 1st level, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your Warlock level (minimum of 1).

features.name: Dark One's Own Luck
features.description: Starting at 6th level, you can call on your patron to alter fate in your favor. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add a d10 to your roll. You can do so after seeing the initial roll but before any of the roll's effects occur. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Fiendish Resilience
features.description: Starting at 10th level, you can choose one damage type when you finish a short or long rest. You gain resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature.

features.name: Hurl Through Hell
features.description: Starting at 14th level, when you hit a creature with an attack, you can use this feature to instantly transport the target through the lower planes. The creature disappears and hurtles through a nightmare landscape. At the end of your next turn, the target returns to the space it previously occupied. The creature takes 10d10 psychic damage as it reels from its horrific experience.

features.name: Expanded Spell List (Archfey)
features.description: Archfey Expanded Spells: 1st: Faerie Fire, Sleep; 2nd: Calm Emotions, Phantasmal Force; 3rd: Blink, Plant Growth; 4th: Dominate Beast, Greater Invisibility; 5th: Dominate Person, Seeming.

features.name: Fey Presence
features.description: Starting at 1st level, your patron bestows upon you the ability to project the beguiling and fearsome presence of the fey. As an action, you can cause each creature in a 10-foot cube originating from you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. The creatures that fail are all charmed or frightened (your choice) until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Misty Escape
features.description: Starting at 6th level, you can vanish in a puff of mist in response to harm. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to turn invisible and teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You remain invisible until the start of your next turn or until you attack or cast a spell.

features.name: Beguiling Defenses
features.description: Beginning at 10th level, your patron teaches you how to turn the mind-affecting magic of your enemies against them. You are immune to being charmed, and when another creature attempts to charm you, you can use your reaction to attempt to turn the charm back on that creature. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC or be charmed by you for 1 minute or until the creature takes any damage.

features.name: Dark Delirium
features.description: Starting at 14th level, you can plunge a creature into an illusory realm. As an action, choose a creature that you can see within 60 feet. It must make a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. On a failed save, it is charmed or frightened (your choice) for 1 minute. Until the spell ends, the creature is under a hallucination of your choosing.

features.name: Expanded Spell List (Great Old One)
features.description: The Great Old One lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a Warlock spell. These spells count as Warlock spells for you and are added to your available spell list. 1st level: Dissonant Whispers, Tasha's Hideous Laughter; 2nd level: Detect Thoughts, Phantasmal Force; 3rd level: Clairvoyance, Sending; 4th level: Dominate Beast, Evard's Black Tentacles; 5th level: Dominate Person, Telekinesis.

features.name: Awakened Mind
features.description: Starting at 1st level, your alien knowledge gives you the ability to touch the minds of other creatures. You can communicate telepathically with any creature you can see within 30 feet. You don't need to share a language, but the creature must be able to understand at least one language.

features.name: Entropic Ward
features.description: At 6th level, you learn to magically ward yourself against attack and turn an enemy's failed strike into good luck for yourself. When a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on that roll. If the attack misses you, your next attack roll against the creature has advantage.

features.name: Thought Shield
features.description: Starting at 10th level, your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or other means unless you allow it. You also have resistance to psychic damage, and whenever a creature deals psychic damage to you, that creature takes the same amount of damage.

features.name: Create Thrall
features.description: At 14th level, you gain the ability to infect a humanoid's mind with the alien magic of your patron. You can use your action to touch an incapacitated humanoid. That creature is then charmed by you until a Remove Curse spell is cast on it or until you use this feature again.

features.name: Expanded Spell List (Celestial)
features.description: Celestial Expanded Spells: 1st: Cure Wounds, Guiding Bolt; 2nd: Flaming Sphere, Lesser Restoration; 3rd: Daylight, Revivify; 4th: Guardian of Faith, Wall of Fire; 5th: Flame Strike, Greater Restoration.

features.name: Bonus Cantrips
features.description: At 1st level, you learn the Light and Sacred Flame cantrips. They count as warlock cantrips for you, but they don't count against your number of cantrips known.

features.name: Healing Light
features.description: At 1st level, you gain the ability to channel celestial energy to heal wounds. You have a pool of d6s that you spend to fuel this healing. The number of dice in the pool equals 1 + your warlock level. As a bonus action, you can heal one creature you can see within 60 feet by spending up to half your warlock level (rounded up) dice from the pool. The creature regains hit points equal to the rolled total. Your pool regains all expended dice when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Radiant Soul
features.description: Starting at 6th level, your link to the Celestial allows you to serve as a conduit for radiant energy. You have resistance to radiant damage, and when you cast a spell that deals radiant or fire damage, you add your Charisma modifier to one radiant or fire damage roll of that spell.

features.name: Celestial Resilience
features.description: Starting at 10th level, you gain temporary hit points whenever you finish a short or long rest. These temporary hit points equal your warlock level + your Charisma modifier. Additionally, choose up to five creatures you can see at the end of the rest. Those creatures each gain temporary hit points equal to half your warlock level + your Charisma modifier.

features.name: Searing Vengeance
features.description: Starting at 14th level, the radiant energy you channel allows you to resist death. When you have to make a death saving throw at the start of your turn, you can instead spring back to your feet with a burst of radiant energy. You regain hit points equal to half your hit point maximum, and then you stand up. Each creature of your choice that is within 30 feet of you takes radiant damage equal to 2d8 + your Charisma modifier.

features.name: Expanded Spell List (Undying)
features.description: Undying Expanded Spells: 1st: False Life, Ray of Sickness; 2nd: Blindness/Deafness, Silence; 3rd: Feign Death, Speak with Dead; 4th: Aura of Life, Death Ward; 5th: Contagion, Legend Lore.

features.name: Among the Dead
features.description: Starting at 1st level, you learn the Spare the Dying cantrip, which counts as a warlock cantrip for you. You also have advantage on saving throws against any disease. Additionally, undead have difficulty harming you. If an undead targets you directly with an attack or a harmful spell, that creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC (an undead needn't make the save when it includes you in an area effect, such as the explosion of fireball).

features.name: Defy Death
features.description: Starting at 6th level, you can give yourself vitality when you cheat death or when you help someone else cheat it. You can regain hit points equal to 1d8 + your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 hit point) when you succeed on a death saving throw or when you stabilize a creature with Spare the Dying.

features.name: Undying Nature
features.description: Beginning at 10th level, you can hold your breath indefinitely, and you don't require food, water, or sleep, although you still require rest to reduce exhaustion and still benefit from finishing short and long rests. In addition, you age at a slower rate. For every 10 years that pass, your body ages only 1 year, and you are immune to being magically aged.

features.name: Indestructible Life
features.description: When you reach 14th level, you partake of some of the true secrets of the Undying. On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d8 + your warlock level. Additionally, if you put a severed body part of yours back in place when you use this feature, the part reattaches.

options.name: Component Pouch
options.description: Spellcasting focus — replaces material components without cost

options.name: Arcane Focus
options.description: Crystal, orb, rod, staff, or wand — spellcasting focus

options.name: Scholar's Pack
options.description: Backpack, book of lore, bottle of ink, ink pen, 10 sheets parchment, bag of sand, small knife

options.name: Dungeoneer's Pack
options.description: Crowbar, hammer, pitons, torches, tinderbox, rations, waterskin, rope

Acolyte.description: You have spent your life in the service of a temple to a specific god or pantheon of gods, acting as an intermediary between the realm of the holy and the mortal world.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency in Insight and Religion.

features.name: Languages
features.description: You can speak, read, and write two additional languages of your choice.

features.name: Shelter of the Faithful
features.description: As an acolyte, you command the respect of those who share your faith and can perform religious ceremonies of your deity. You and your companions can expect free healing and care at a temple of your faith, though you must provide material components for spells. Those who share your religion will support you at a modest lifestyle. You might have a residence at a specific temple where you have a home.

startingItems.name: Holy Symbol
startingItems.description: A holy symbol of your deity

Charlatan.description: You have always had a way with people. You know what makes them tick, you can tease out their hearts desires after a few minutes of conversation, and with a few leading questions you can read them like they were children's books.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency in Deception and Sleight of Hand.

features.name: Tool Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency with a disguise kit and a forgery kit.

features.name: False Identity
features.description: You have created a second identity including documentation, established acquaintances, and disguises. You can also forge documents including official papers and personal letters, as long as you have seen an example of the kind of document or handwriting you are trying to copy.

startingItems.name: Con tools
startingItems.description: Ten stoppered bottles, set of weighted dice, deck of marked cards, or signet ring of an imaginary duke

Criminal.description: You are an experienced criminal with a history of breaking the law. You have spent a lot of time among other criminals and still have contacts within the criminal underworld.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency in Deception and Stealth.

features.name: Gaming Set
features.description: You gain proficiency with one type of gaming set of your choice.

features.name: Thieves Tools
features.description: You gain proficiency with thieves tools.

features.name: Criminal Contact
features.description: You have a reliable and trustworthy contact who acts as your liaison to a network of other criminals. You know how to get messages to and from your contact, even over great distances, through messengers, corrupt caravan masters, and seedy sailors.

Entertainer.description: You thrive in front of an audience. You know how to entrance them, entertain them, and even inspire them. Your poetics can stir the hearts of those who hear you, awakening grief or joy, laughter or anger.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency in Acrobatics and Performance.

features.name: Musical Instrument
features.description: You gain proficiency with one musical instrument of your choice.

features.name: Disguise Kit
features.description: You gain proficiency with a disguise kit.

features.name: By Popular Demand
features.description: You can always find a place to perform, usually in an inn or tavern but possibly with a circus, theatre, or noble's court. You receive free lodging and food of a modest or comfortable standard as long as you perform each night. Your performance makes you something of a local figure wherever you have performed.

startingItems.name: The favor of an admirer
startingItems.description: Love letter, lock of hair, or trinket

Folk Hero.description: You come from a humble social rank, but you are destined for so much more. Already the people of your home village regard you as their champion, and your destiny calls you to stand against the tyrants and monsters that threaten the common folk everywhere.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency in Animal Handling and Survival.

features.name: Artisans Tools
features.description: You gain proficiency with one type of artisan's tools of your choice.

features.name: Vehicles (Land)
features.description: You gain proficiency with vehicles (land).

features.name: Rustic Hospitality
features.description: Since you come from the ranks of the common folk, you fit in among them with ease. You can find a place to hide, rest, or recuperate among other commoners, unless you have shown yourself to be a danger to them. They will shield you from the law or anyone else searching for you, though they will not risk their lives for you.

Hermit.description: You lived in seclusion either in a sheltered community such as a monastery, or entirely alone for a formative part of your life. In your time apart from the clamour of society, you found quiet, solitude, and perhaps some of the answers you were looking for.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency in Medicine and Religion.

features.name: Herbalism Kit
features.description: You gain proficiency with an herbalism kit.

features.name: Language
features.description: You can speak, read, and write one additional language of your choice.

features.name: Discovery
features.description: The quiet seclusion of your extended hermitage gave you access to a unique and powerful discovery. The exact nature of this revelation is up to you and your DM, but it might be a great truth about the cosmos, the deities, the powerful beings of the outer planes, or the forces of nature. It might be a site that no one else has ever seen, or a fact long forgotten, or a relic of the past that could rewrite history.

startingItems.name: Scroll case with notes
startingItems.description: Notes from your studies or prayers

Noble.description: You understand wealth, power, and privilege. You carry a noble title, and your family owns land, collects taxes, and wields significant political influence.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency in History and Persuasion.

features.name: Gaming Set
features.description: You gain proficiency with one type of gaming set of your choice.

features.name: Language
features.description: You can speak, read, and write one additional language of your choice.

features.name: Position of Privilege
features.description: Thanks to your noble birth, people are inclined to think the best of you. You are welcome in high society, and people assume you have the right to be wherever you are. The common folk make every effort to accommodate you, and other people of high birth treat you as a member of the same social sphere. You can secure an audience with a local noble if you need to.

Outlander.description: You grew up in the wilds, far from civilisation and the comforts of town and technology. You have witnessed the migration of herds larger than forests and survived weather more extreme than any city-dweller could comprehend.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency in Athletics and Survival.

features.name: Musical Instrument
features.description: You gain proficiency with one musical instrument of your choice.

features.name: Language
features.description: You can speak, read, and write one additional language of your choice.

features.name: Wanderer
features.description: You have an excellent memory for maps and geography, and you can always recall the general layout of terrain, settlements, and other features around you. In addition, you can find food and fresh water for yourself and up to five other people each day, provided that the land offers berries, small game, water, and so forth.

Sage.description: You spent years learning the lore of the multiverse. You scoured manuscripts, studied under sages, and pored over anything you could get your hands on. Your efforts have paid off with a wealth of arcane knowledge.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: Choose any 2 skills to be proficient in.

features.name: Languages
features.description: You can speak, read, and write two additional languages of your choice.

features.name: Researcher
features.description: When you attempt to learn or recall a piece of lore, if you do not know that information, you often know where and from whom you can obtain it. Usually this comes from a library, scriptorium, university, or sage. Your DM might rule that the knowledge you seek is secreted away in an almost inaccessible place, or that it simply cannot be found. Unearthing the deepest secrets of the multiverse can require an adventure or even a whole campaign.

Sailor.description: You sailed on a seagoing vessel for years. In that time, you faced down mighty storms, monsters of the deep, and those who wanted to sink your craft to the bottomless depths.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency in Athletics and Perception.

features.name: Navigators Tools
features.description: You gain proficiency with navigator's tools.

features.name: Vehicles (Water)
features.description: You gain proficiency with vehicles (water).

features.name: Ships Passage
features.description: When you need to, you can secure free passage on a sailing ship for yourself and your adventuring companions. You might sail on the ship you served on, or another ship you have good relations with. In return for your free passage, you and your companions are expected to assist the crew during the voyage.

Soldier.description: War has been your life for as long as you care to remember. You trained as a youth, studied the use of weapons and armor, and learned basic survival techniques, including how to stay alive on the battlefield.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency in Athletics and Intimidation.

features.name: Gaming Set
features.description: You gain proficiency with one type of gaming set of your choice.

features.name: Vehicles (Land)
features.description: You gain proficiency with vehicles (land).

features.name: Military Rank
features.description: You have a military rank from your career as a soldier. Soldiers loyal to your former military organisation still recognise your authority and influence, and defer to you if they are of a lower rank. You can invoke your rank to exert influence over other soldiers and requisition simple equipment or horses for temporary use. You can usually gain access to friendly military encampments and fortresses where your rank is recognised.

startingItems.name: Trophy from fallen enemy
startingItems.description: Dagger, broken blade, or piece of a banner

startingItems.name: Deck of cards or set of dice

Urchin.description: You grew up on the streets alone, orphaned, and poor. You had no one to watch over you or to provide for you, so you learned to provide for yourself. You fought fiercely over food and kept a constant watch out for other desperate souls who might take what you had.

features.name: Skill Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency in Sleight of Hand and Stealth.

features.name: Disguise Kit
features.description: You gain proficiency with a disguise kit.

features.name: Thieves Tools
features.description: You gain proficiency with thieves tools.

features.name: City Secrets
features.description: You know the secret patterns and flow to cities and can find passages through the urban sprawl that others would miss. When you are not in combat, you (and companions you lead) can travel between any two locations in the city twice as fast as your speed would normally allow.

spells.name: Fire Bolt
spells.description: A mote of fire hurls toward a creature. Make a ranged spell attack. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 fire damage. A flammable object hit by this spell ignites if it isn't being worn or carried. Damage increases to 2d10 at 5th level, 3d10 at 11th, and 4d10 at 17th.

spells.name: Mage Hand
spells.description: A spectral, floating hand appears at a point you choose within range. The hand lasts for the duration or until you dismiss it as an action. The hand vanishes if it is ever more than 30 feet from you or if you cast this spell again. You can use the hand to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.

combat.notes: Spectral hand manipulates objects up to 10 lbs

spells.name: Prestidigitation
spells.description: This spell is a minor magical trick that novice spellcasters use for practice. You create one of the following magical effects: a harmless sensory effect, light or snuff a flame, clean or soil an object, chill/warm/flavor food, make a colour/mark/symbol appear, or create a small trinket or illusory image.

combat.notes: Minor magical trick; countless minor effects

spells.name: Ray of Frost
